newsitem.title: INDIA: India sees $7.5 bln foreign investment in 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: India sees $7.5 bln foreign investment in 1996/97.

text.p: Finance Minister P.Chidambaram said on Friday that India expected to receive a total of $7.5 billion in 1996/97 (April-March) in three categories of foreign investment.
Chidambaram told parliament that India needed $17 billion during the year for repayment of debt amounting to $10 billion bridging a current foreign trade deficit of $7.0 billion.
India would receive around $9.5 billion from commercial borrowings, foreign aid and deposits from expatriate Indians during the year, Chidambaram said.
"The remaining $7.5 billion must come from foreign direct investment (FDI), foreign institutional investors (FIIs) and global depositary receipt (GDR) inflows," he said.
Of these, $3.0 to $3.5 billion was expected from FDI, $3.0 billion from FIIs, and $1.5 billion from the issue of GDRs (overseas shares) by Indian companies, Chidambaram said.
The $10 billion India needs for repayment of debt includes $2.2 billion for redemption of India Development Bonds (IDBs) five years ago during a balance of payments crisis, he said.
"This year, we cannot afford to run down our (foreign exchange) reserves," Chidambaram told parliament. "We need more foreign capital."
He said Industry Minister Murasoli Maran had cleared all the backlog of applications for foreign investment pending in his ministry, which oversees the Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB).
